examples.en: I asked the person in charge of classes about the application date.

examples.ko: 담당자가 자리에 없어서 다시 전화하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The person in charge wasn't at their desk, so they told me to call back.
Please give me the contact details of the person in charge.
The person in charge of this job has changed.

examples.ko: 담당자가 누구예요? — 이번 달부터 제가 맡고 있어요.
examples.en: Who is in charge? — I've been handling it since this month.

explain: 이메일에서 누가 담당인지 모를 때 “담당자님께”라고 시작해요. 이름을 몰라도 쓸 수 있는 정중한 인사예요.

dict_examples.en: To inquire with the person in charge.

explain_en: When you don't know who handles something, start an email with “담당자님께” (To the person in charge). It's a polite opening that works without a name.

examples.en: The application deadline is five o'clock today.

examples.ko: 보고서 마감이 내일이라서 오늘 밤을 새워야 해요.
examples.en: The report is due tomorrow, so I'll have to stay up all night.

examples.ko: 마감이 얼마 안 남아서 정말 바빠요.
examples.en: There isn't much time before the deadline, so I'm really busy.
Make sure to submit it before the deadline.
When is the deadline? — This Friday.

explain: 신청 자리가 다 차도 “마감됐어요”라고 해요. 시간이 끝난 것만 말하는 게 아니에요.
explain_en: You also say “마감됐어요” when all the spots are full. It doesn't only mean the time is over.

examples.en: Write your name and address on the application form.

examples.ko: 회사 홈페이지에서 휴가 신청 양식을 내려받으세요.
examples.en: Download the leave request form from the company website.

examples.ko: 이력서 양식은 회사 홈페이지에서 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get the résumé form on the company's website.

examples.ko: 이 양식대로 쓰지 않으면 다시 써야 해요.
examples.en: If you don't write it in this format, you have to write it again.

examples.ko: 보고서 형식이 있어요? — 네, 이 양식에 맞춰 쓰세요.
examples.en: Is there a report format? — Yes, please follow this template.

explain: 소리가 같은 양식(洋食)은 서양 음식이에요. 문서 양식과 헷갈리지 마세요.

dict_examples.en: Prepare the documents to match the form.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Submit the report according to the given format.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 양식이 맞지 않으면 컴퓨터가 데이터를 읽지 못한다.
dict_examples.en: If the format doesn't match, the computer can't read the data.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: A word that sounds the same, 양식 (洋食), means Western food. Don't mix it up with the 양식 for documents.

examples.ko: 책을 늦게 반납하면 벌금이 있다고 했어요.
examples.en: They said there's a fine if you return a book late.
I parked in the wrong spot and had to pay a fine.

examples.ko: 우리 모임은 지각하면 벌금이 오천 원이에요.
examples.en: In our group, being late costs a 5,000 won fine.
The fine was so expensive that I was shocked.

examples.ko: 벌금은 어디에서 내요? — 은행이나 인터넷으로 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Where do I pay the fine? — You can pay at a bank or online.

explain: 법원이 정하는 돈이 원래 벌금이에요. 일상에서는 주차나 지각 같은 규칙 위반으로 내는 돈도 벌금이라고 많이 말해요.

dict_examples.en: To pay a fine.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: To be sentenced to a fine of up to 5 million won.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: A 벌금 is originally money set by a court. In daily life, people often also use it for money paid for breaking rules, like bad parking or being late.

examples.en: If there's a fire, get outside immediately.
If anything goes wrong, contact me right away.
Please reply right away when you get the email.

examples.ko: 카드는 신청하면 즉시 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use the card as soon as you apply.

examples.ko: 아픈 사람이 생기면 즉시 구급차를 부르세요.
examples.en: If someone gets sick, call an ambulance immediately.

explain: 말할 때는 “바로”를 많이 쓰고, 안내문이나 규정에는 “즉시”가 많이 나와요.

dict_examples.en: To answer immediately.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: In speech, people often say “바로”. On notices and in regulations, you will see “즉시” more often.

examples.ko: 팀장님이 지금 당장 회의실 불을 끄라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The team leader told us to turn off the meeting room lights right now.

examples.ko: 배가 너무 고파서 당장 뭐라도 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'm so hungry I want to eat something right now.

examples.ko: 시험이 내일이라서 당장 공부를 시작해야 해요.
examples.en: The exam is tomorrow, so I have to start studying right now.
I can't buy it right now because I don't have the money.

examples.ko: 언제까지 해야 해요? — 당장 하지 않아도 돼요. 내일까지만 하세요.
examples.en: By when do I have to do it? — You don't have to do it right now. Just finish by tomorrow.

explain: “당장은 …”은 지금 상황만 말하는 느낌이에요. 나중에는 달라질 수 있다는 뜻이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: “당장은 …” talks only about the situation right now. It hints that things may be different later.

p.n: 바로 is neutral; 당장 stresses urgency.

examples.en: The teacher told everyone to come on time.
Traffic was bad, so I didn't make it on time.
The train left on time.
The meeting has to start on time.

examples.ko: 제시간에 올 수 있어요? — 네, 늦지 않게 갈게요.
examples.en: Can you come on time? — Yes, I won't be late.

explain: 제시간은 띄어 쓰지 않고 한 단어로 써요. 비슷한 말로 “제때”가 있어요. “약을 제때 먹어요”처럼 써요.

dict_examples.en: To arrive on time.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: To finish the work on time.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 제시간 is written as one word, without a space. A similar word is “제때”: “약을 제때 먹어요” (take your medicine on time).

examples.ko: 도서관 책 반납은 다음 주 월요일까지예요.
examples.en: The library book return is due by next Monday.
You can return the rental car at the airport.

examples.ko: 공유 자전거는 반납 전에 자물쇠를 꼭 잠가야 해요.
examples.en: With shared bikes, you must lock them before returning them.
Please return the umbrella you borrowed by tomorrow.
Is today the return date? — No, it's tomorrow.

explain: 도서관, 렌터카처럼 빌린 곳에 돌려줄 때 반납을 써요. 친구한테 빌린 물건은 보통 “돌려주다”라고 해요.
explain_en: Use 반납 when you give something back to the place you borrowed it from, like a library or a rental car. For things borrowed from a friend, 돌려주다 is more usual.

en: to leave (something) with someone, to entrust

examples.en: Please leave large bags at the storage room by the entrance.

examples.ko: 여행 가는 동안 강아지를 친구에게 맡겼어요.
examples.en: While I was away, I left my dog with a friend.
I left my winter coat at the dry cleaner's.
Please leave this job to me.
Leave the key with the security office.

explain: 맡긴 물건을 가져올 때는 “찾다”를 써요. 세탁소에 맡기고 내일 찾아요.

phrases.en: to let oneself go with (music, the waves, etc.)
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 아니라 몸을 흐름에 자연스럽게 따르게 할 때
phrases.nuance_en: not about objects: used when you let yourself follow the flow of something
phrases.en_equiv: to let oneself go with (music, the waves, etc.)

explain_en: When you pick up what you left, the verb is 찾다: you 맡기다 your clothes at the cleaner's and 찾다 them tomorrow.

en: to make sure to take, to pack

examples.en: Make sure you bring your laptop tomorrow.

examples.ko: 엄마가 항상 제 도시락을 챙겨 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mom always packed my lunch for me.

examples.ko: 비가 올 것 같으니까 우산을 챙겨 가세요.
examples.en: It looks like rain, so take an umbrella with you.

examples.ko: 친구 생일을 챙겨서 케이크를 사 갔어요.
examples.en: I remembered my friend's birthday and brought a cake.
Did you pack your passport? — Yes, it's in my bag.

explain: 챙기다는 잊지 않고 준비한다는 느낌이에요. 가져갈 물건뿐 아니라 먹는 것, 건강 같은 것도 챙길 수 있어요.

dict_examples.ko: 나는 세면도구를 챙겨 들고 바깥으로 나왔다.

explain_en: 챙기다 has the feeling of not forgetting and getting something ready. You can 챙기다 not only things to take, but also meals and health.
